paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.German: This plot illustrates the relationship between rank and error. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” with a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at intervals of 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is labeled "Errors (COPA)" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. A single green line with circular markers is present, representing error values at each rank. The line begins at a value of approximately 0.22 at a rank of 4, decreases to approximately 0.17 at a rank of 16, then increases to approximately 0.34 at a rank of 64, and finally plateaus at approximately 0.33 for a rank of 256. Error bars are shown at each Rank point, displaying a range of approximately ±0.05.
